reason: Start building rocky planetesimals by letting the stone and metal grains stick in gentle collisions.
expectation: I expect a larger rocky aggregate, though further steps will be needed for a planetesimal.

alternatives.reason: I also considered starting with icy grains, but chose the rocky goal first.

effect: Rocky pebbles have formed, but simple sticking alone will not keep growing them reliably.
reaction: The bouncing and fragmentation barrier makes the next stage interesting.
reason: Continue the rocky path by applying gas drag to the pebbles.
expectation: I expect gas drag to change how the pebbles move through the disk, perhaps helping them gather; the exact result is uncertain.

alternatives.reason: I considered starting the icy path, but prefer to follow the rocky pebbles further first.

effect: Gas drag makes the rocky pebbles drift, potentially concentrating them in structured regions.
reaction: The link between gas drag and orbital drift is interesting.
reason: Use the pressure maximum to try to gather the drifting pebbles.
expectation: I expect the pressure maximum to concentrate the pebbles into a denser swarm, though gravity may still be needed.

alternatives.reason: I considered starting the icy path, but want to follow the rocky pebbles toward concentration first.

effect: The pressure maximum gathered rocky solids into a dense swarm, bypassing continual growth through sticking.
reaction: It's satisfying to see how concentration gets around the collision barrier.
reason: Apply gravity to the dense swarm to advance the rocky planetesimal goal.
expectation: I expect the swarm to collapse into rocky planetesimals, though the exact result is uncertain.

alternatives.reason: I considered starting the icy path, but the rocky swarm is ready for gravity.

effect: Gravity collapsed the rocky swarm into planetesimals, completing the rocky goal; the icy goal remains.
reaction: The gravitational collapse neatly completes the rocky sequence.
reason: Start the icy path with the only offered combination.
expectation: I expect gentle collisions to form icy pebbles or aggregates, analogous to the rocky path.

effect: The icy material formed pebbles carrying both rock and volatiles; the icy planetesimal goal remains.
reaction: The parallel with the rocky path is clear, though somewhat repetitive.
reason: Apply gas drag to the icy pebbles, the only offered combination.
expectation: I expect the icy pebbles to drift, as the rocky pebbles did.

effect: Gas drag concentrated the icy solids through collective feedback, a different route from the rocky pressure trap; the swarm is now ready for gravity.
reaction: The streaming instability is a welcome distinction from the rocky sequence.
reason: Apply gravity to the icy swarm; this is the only offered combination and should advance the remaining goal.
expectation: I expect the concentrated swarm to collapse into icy planetesimals, as gravity did for the rocky swarm.

effect: Gravity bound the icy swarm into planetesimals, completing the remaining goal; they are possible water carriers, not the only source of terrestrial hydrogen.
reaction: The parallel conclusion was predictable, but the water-carrier qualification was useful.

mostWorthwhile.text: Concentrating rocky pebbles at a pressure maximum was most worthwhile: it showed a way around the barrier to continual sticking.

leastWorthwhile.text: Starting the icy route felt repetitive after making rocky pebbles, though it set up a different concentration mechanism.

surprise.text: Gas drag concentrated the icy swarm through collective feedback and streaming instability, rather than repeating the rocky pressure-trap route.

arbitrary.text: No action felt entirely purposeless, although the fast menu supplied compatible choices rather than letting me discover them.

continue.text: I would continue: the distinct ways solids concentrate made me curious how these planetesimals become larger worlds.
